author: Louis B. Wright
title: The Noble Savage of Madagascar in 1640
role_description: Non-Western locale/people as object in European noble-savage representation
interpretive_note: Early Africa presence must not be coded as African intellectual history; it is a history of European/colonial representation.

author: Donald F. Lach
title: Leibniz and China
role_description: China/Chinese knowledge as source/contact field within a European canonical thinker's intellectual history
interpretive_note: Strong early China entry, but historiographical address remains Leibniz/Europe.

author: Elizabeth Flower
title: The Mexican Revolt Against Positivism
role_description: Local actors reject/rework an imported intellectual programme; region treated as a site of intellectual change
interpretive_note: Important pre-Zea evidence that Latin-American reception/revolt could already be written as JHI intellectual history.

author: Herrlee Glessner Creel
title: Sinism--A Clarification
role_description: Debate over how Chinese thought/culture should be conceptually classified in a comparative framework
interpretive_note: Do not infer exact target until article text is read; title/context places China inside a conceptual-methodological dispute.

author: Arthur F. Wright
title: Professor Northrop's Chapter on the Traditional Culture of the Orient
role_description: Review-discussion evaluating a large comparative model of 'Oriental' traditional culture
interpretive_note: Shows area specialist policing the validity of broad East/West synthesis inside JHI.

author: Mary Wyman
title: Chinese Mysticism and Wordsworth
role_description: Chinese intellectual/religious materials connected to a European literary genealogy
interpretive_note: Continuation of China-as-source/antecedent role before the 1951 reaction symposium.

author: R. C. Bald
title: Sir William Chambers and the Chinese Garden
role_description: Chinese garden/aesthetic material reconstructed through British reception
interpretive_note: Non-Western object enters via cultural translation/reception in Europe.

author: Joseph Needham
title: Human Laws and Laws of Nature in China and the West (I)
role_description: China and West treated as co-comparable intellectual traditions around law/nature
interpretive_note: Issue-opening placement marks stronger parity of comparative address than 1935 supplementary India.

author: Arthur F. Wright
title: Fu I and the Rejection of Buddhism
role_description: Chinese actor rejects imported Buddhism; recipient society is active intellectual agent
interpretive_note: Key move from Asia-as-source-for-Europe to non-Western recipient/rejecter of imported ideas.

author: Hellmut Wilhelm
title: The Problem of Within and without, a Confucian Attempt in Syncretism
role_description: Chinese intellectual system actively reorganizes outside/inside materials through syncretism
interpretive_note: Same symposium operationalizes syncretism rather than passive diffusion.

author: Benjamin Schwartz
title: Ch'en Tu-Hsiu and the Acceptance of the Modern West
role_description: Chinese actor's selective acceptance of imported modern Western ideas
interpretive_note: Modern reception history; later becomes foundational China intellectual-history scholarship.

author: Ernest A. Moody
title: Galileo and Avempace: The Dynamics of the Leaning Tower Experiment (I)
role_description: Arabic/Islamic philosopher reconstructed as a technically significant antecedent/intermediary in European science history
interpretive_note: Arabic thought enters deeply and technically, but the narrative address is still Galileo/European scientific genealogy.

author: Ernest A. Moody
title: Galileo and Avempace: The Dynamics of the Leaning Tower Experiment (II)
role_description: Continuation of Avempace/Galileo source and dynamics reconstruction
interpretive_note: Long two-part treatment shows substantial Arabic technical source-work inside JHI.

author: Roy Harvey Pearce
title: The 'Ruines of Mankind': The Indian and the Puritan Mind
role_description: Indigenous figure as symbolic/intellectual object in Puritan thought; links representation to colonial cultural process
interpretive_note: Do not conflate 'Indian' with South Asia; this is Pearce's savagism/colonial-representation programme.

author: P. T. Raju
title: The Development of Indian Thought
role_description: Indian philosophy narrated as an internally developing intellectual tradition from Vedic/Upanishadic roots onward
interpretive_note: Major regime marker: by 1952 India is no longer only supplementary/comparative evidence; a South Asian intellectual tradition is itself the historical subject.

author: Richard M. Morse
title: Toward a Theory of Spanish American Government
role_description: Regional political-intellectual structures treated as an internally analyzable historical field
interpretive_note: Strengthens Latin-American regional intellectual/political history before later Zea convergence.

author: Buddha Prakash
title: The Hindu Philosophy of History
role_description: Hindu historical thought/philosophy treated directly as an intellectual tradition
interpretive_note: Confirms 1952 Raju is not an isolated one-off; South Asian internal intellectual history recurs in JHI.
